workstream: Indian public education funding, institutional coverage and access-change research

coverage.scopeWarning: A researched source registry and selected extracted official series, not exhaustive funding or closure coverage for every city.

sources.title: Closure of Government Schools — Lok Sabha Unstarred Question 1374
sources.geographicScope: India; all 36 states and union territories; all 75 Uttar Pradesh districts
claims: Annexure I reports government-school stock counts for five academic years by state/UT.
Annexure II reports government-school stock counts for all Uttar Pradesh districts.
India government schools: 1,022,386 in 2021-22 and 1,005,245 in 2025-26.
NEP paragraph 7.4 says consolidation should only proceed when access is unaffected.
limitations: The answer provides stock counts, not a school-by-school closure or merger register.
Districts are not cities or school catchments.
No matched population series or causal impact evaluation is provided.
Reported by states/UTs through UDISE+.
sources.locator: PDF page4, Annexure I; pages5–6, Annexure II

sources.title: Declining Enrolment of Students in Government Schools in Uttar Pradesh — Lok Sabha Question 2445
sources.period: Funding FY 2023-24 to FY 2025-26; schools 2014-15 to 2025-26
sources.geographicScope: India and states/UTs; funding Uttar Pradesh; school counts Shamli district
claims: Provides approved central and actual released central shares for Uttar Pradesh Samagra Shiksha and PM SHRI for three financial years.
Shamli district government-school counts rise from 621 in 2021-22 to 623 in 2025-26.
limitations: The requested district spending is answered with state-level approved/released figures; do not label these district spending.
Releases are not expenditure, audited utilisation, or money received by an individual school.
Annexures contain government-school counts, not verified closure events.

sources.title: Ministry of Education releases UDISE+ 2024-25 report
sources.publisher: Ministry of Education / Press Information Bureau
claims: Reports 104,125 single-teacher schools and 7,993 zero-enrolment schools in 2024-25.
Reports total teachers 10,122,420.
Reports computer access in 64.7% and internet in 63.5% of schools.
limitations: National aggregate with mixed management categories; not a city-level finding.
A zero-enrolment school is not necessarily a closed school.
2025-26 official parliamentary school-count data is newer.

sources.title: Report on UDISE+ 2023-24 — existing structure
sources.evidenceStatus: Primary source fetched; methodology also present in search extract
claims: Separates government, government-aided, private unaided recognised, and other schools.
Reports that student-wise collection from 2022-23 is not strictly comparable with earlier aggregate reporting for several education indicators.
limitations: Historical methodology reference; not latest school data.
Population denominator moderation can affect ratio comparisons.
UDISE listing alone does not confer recognition.

sources.title: AISHE Final Reports
claims: Lists 2023-24 and 2022-23 final reports and Excel files.
limitations: Index page is a discovery source, not a transaction or district funding ledger.

sources.title: Union Ministry releases AISHE 2022-23 and 2023-24 reports
sources.publisher: Ministry of Education / Press Information Bureau
claims: For 2023-24, 59,533 of 64,756 registered HEIs participated.
Higher education enrolment is reported as 4.50 crore in 2023-24.
GER is 30 in 2023-24 and uses ages 18-23 population projections based on Census 2011.
limitations: Participation is voluntary and data is self-reported by institutions.
Registration, survey response and estimated enrolment have different denominators.
Report reference period differs from publication date.

sources.title: AISHE Report 2023-24
sources.publisher: Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Education
claims: 48,246 colleges were registered and 46,468 responded.
Of responding colleges, 17.1% were government, 12.9% private aided and 70.0% private unaided.
Contains state tables for private/government colleges and district distribution.
limitations: Responding-college percentages must not be applied as exact counts to all registered colleges.
Institution prevalence is not a funding share.

sources.title: Chhattisgarh Samagra Shiksha 2025-26 revised PAB minutes
sources.publisher: Department of School Education and Literacy, Ministry of Education
sources.evidenceStatus: Official indexed PDF extract retrieved through Exa; origin direct fetch HTTP404
claims: Approved annual work plan: ₹232,029.17 lakh including ₹82,492.13 lakh spillover.
Planned central share to be released: ₹112,900.28 lakh; corresponding state share ₹75,267.52 lakh.
Supplementary ICT labs and smart classrooms approval: ₹14,133.80 lakh.
limitations: Supersedes sections of earlier 9 May 2025 minutes; preserve version history.
The section heading says Actual Release, but the line explicitly says to be released: classify as planned/approved, not actual disbursement.
Opening balances and spillover make the approved plan different from fresh allocations.
OCR affects table layout; use explicit prose figures and reconcile original PDF before bulk extraction.
Origin PDF returned HTTP404 on2026-10-06; preserve indexed-text access status and locate replacement archive before treating as live-verified.

sources.title: Cabinet approves PM SHRI Schools
sources.evidenceStatus: Primary source fetched; date corroborated by Ministry scheme page
claims: Total project cost ₹27,360 crore, including central share ₹18,128 crore, over five years.
Targets more than 14,500 existing schools managed by central/state/UT/local government.
Selection uses eligibility checks and challenge mode.
limitations: Multi-year programme outlay is not current-year expenditure or total India education funding.
Not a grant programme for all private unaided schools.
National targets do not verify city-level awards.

sources.title: PM Schools for Rising India — scheme information
claims: At the page's update, 12,079 schools had been selected through four phases.
Confirms ₹27,360 crore total and ₹18,128 crore central project cost.
limitations: Selection snapshot is dated November 2024 and must not be labelled current in October 2026.

sources.title: PM-USHA Guidelines
sources.publisher: Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Education
claims: Covers government and government-aided higher education institutions of states/UTs.
Gives priority to focus districts and defines components and eligibility.
limitations: Eligibility and programme scope do not establish that an institution has received funding.
Historical AISHE figures in the guidelines are not current counts.

sources.title: PM-USHA: Building Stronger Institutions for a Knowledge-Driven Future
sources.publisher: Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Education
claims: Scheme outlay ₹12,926.10 crore for 2023-24 to 2025-26.
First two PAB meetings approved 440 units worth ₹5,613.12 crore.
FY 2025-26 budget stated as ₹1,815 crore.
Eight new model degree college units approved across Nagaland (4), Manipur (2), Meghalaya (2), totaling ₹119.98 crore.
limitations: Outlay, PAB approvals and annual budget are distinct stages and cannot be added together.
A unit is not necessarily a unique institution.
Snapshot is May 2025; not live allocations.

sources.title: Population Projections for India and States 2011–2036
sources.publisher: National Commission on Population, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare; government mirror by Chhattisgarh DES
sources.geographicScope: India; states and UTs, not official city-level estimates
claims: Uses Census 2011, SRS fertility/mortality and migration assumptions.
Projects total population increase and a decline in the national population aged 5–14 during 2011–2036.
limitations: Projections are model-based rather than new census observations.
Total population growth cannot substitute for school-age population growth.
District/city downscaling requires separate validation.
Mirrored copies surfaced differing summary totals; numeric population claims are intentionally omitted until document edition provenance is reconciled.

sources.title: Five years, 10 states: Where India's government school count fell the most
claims: Reports uneven state-level net school-count reductions and warns against reading stock differences as a simple linear demographic story.
limitations: Secondary lead, not proof of individual closures or wrongdoing.
Do not import the headline as a closure-event count.

sources.title: No merger for schools with 50 or more students as Uttar Pradesh government revises plan
claims: Reports minister's clarification excluding schools with 50 or more students and schools farther than 1km from pairing.
Reports minister saying UDISE codes remain unchanged, buildings may host Bal Vatikas, and original classes can resume if enrolment/capacity warrants.
limitations: Reported policy and explanation, not independent verification of implementation.
Do not turn nearly 10,000 proposed pairings into confirmed permanent closures.
Preserved codes mean stock series can miss changes in where teaching takes place.

sources.title: UP govt tells HC: No merger if school has over 50 students, 1km distance
sources.geographicScope: Sitapur district, Uttar Pradesh; state policy
claims: Reports extension of interim status quo for school pairing in Sitapur until 1 September 2025.
Reports government assurances on enrolment/distance and court clarification that interim order does not affect overall policy.
limitations: Historical interim procedural status, not current case disposition.
Later court orders must be obtained before stating present legality or operative stay.

sources.title: Karnataka rolls out project to merge government schools with KPS magnet schools
sources.geographicScope: Honganuru, Channapatna taluk, Bengaluru South district, Karnataka
claims: Reports a seven-school pilot linked to Honganuru KPS.
Quotes circular instructions on student transfers and transport arrangements.
Reports concern from educationists/student organisations about rural access.
limitations: Underlying circular not retrieved in this pass.
Announced/proposed state scale is not completed implementation.
Allegation that a much larger number of schools would close is not adopted as a fact.

sources.title: Government urged to withdraw order allowing merger of low-enrolment schools
claims: Reports minister's statement that government has no plans to shut any government school.
Reports AIDSO seeking withdrawal of a merger clause and a written assurance.
limitations: Capture minister's denial alongside access concerns.
School closure, transfer of classes and administrative merger may refer to different units.
No inference of dishonesty or wrongdoing.

sources.title: 100 schools with zero enrolment denotified, 120 merged
sources.geographicScope: Himachal Pradesh, including Kangra, Mandi and Shimla districts
claims: Reports 100 zero-enrolment primary/middle schools denotified and 120 primary schools with five or fewer students merged.
Reports difficult-terrain and tribal-area schools were exempted from merger.
limitations: Original school-wise notifications not obtained.
Counts refer to different administrative actions and should remain separate.
Zero enrolment and low enrolment are the official rationale reported; no matched catchment population evidence establishes a contradiction.

sources.title: Krishna Kumari and others v State of UP — 2025:AHC-LKO:38113
sources.evidenceStatus: Official text fetched through Exa; direct origin returned HTTP429 on audit
claims: Paragraph3 identifies Government Order16June2025 and consequent24June2025 list of105 schools challenged in petitions.
limitations: Exa extract reviewed through early statutory discussion; final disposition not independently extracted.
Subsequent appeal reporting exists; do not present this as final current case status.

sources.title: Documents & Reports — Samagra Shiksha PAB minutes
sources.publisher: Department of School Education and Literacy, Ministry of Education
sources.period: Annual state plans; retrieved index includes FY2025-26
sources.evidenceStatus: Official indexed content fetched through Exa
claims: Provides state/UT financial-year entries with minutes, supplementary minutes, addenda and revisions.
limitations: An index to retrieve further records, not extracted transaction coverage.
Document links may move; origin link health must be checked.
Index includes organisations as well as states, so row count is not geographic coverage.

sources.title: Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
sources.publisher: Government of India / Ministry of Education
sources.geographicScope: India, subject to applicability and state implementation rules
sources.evidenceStatus: Official indexed PDF text fetched through Exa
claims: Section12(1)(c) provides entry-level admissions for eligible disadvantaged/weaker-section children of at least25% in specified categories of schools.
Section12(2) provides private unaided school reimbursement capped at state per-child expenditure or actual charge, whichever is lower, with provisos for pre-existing free-education obligations.
limitations: Not an unrestricted private-school capital grant.
School eligibility, constitutional/applicability exclusions, neighbourhood rules and claims are determined by applicable law and state implementation.
Statutory eligibility is not evidence of payment.

sources.title: Quota for EWS Seats in Private Unaided Schools — Lok Sabha Question1260
sources.evidenceStatus: Primary source text fetched through Exa
claims: Provides sanctioned and reimbursed-to-school amounts under RTE for Karnataka for five years.
FY2025-26 sanctioned ₹156.10crore and reimbursed ₹148.68crore.
Government says reimbursement is timely, based on information from the state.
Describes2018 Karnataka neighbourhood-school exemption.
limitations: Including Bengaluru does not make this city-level funding.
The table covers the reimbursement claim population; do not interpret as uniquely new entry-grade admissions without checking definitions.
Sanctioned less reimbursed does not establish overdue obligations or misuse.
Distinct from central releases to the state; do not sum with Samagra central share as independent money.

leads.title: Ghaziabad district: reconcile fewer reported schools with catchment demand
leads.evidence: Government-school stock declined from 504 in 2021-22 to 474 in 2025-26; 493 to 474 in the last year.
leads.classification: Investigation lead; population comparison not verified
missing: Same-boundary child population and migration estimates
leads.nextStep: Match school IDs and administrative orders, then compare 6–14 population and accessible public seats within the same catchments.
leads.claimNotEstablished: Closures despite rising child population or denial of access.

leads.title: Jhansi district: identify the schools behind the count change
leads.evidence: Government-school stock fell from 1,504 in 2021-22 to 1,450 in 2025-26; 1,489 to 1,450 in the last year.
missing: Enrolment and attendance at receiving schools
leads.nextStep: Review 39 net fewer reported schools in 2025-26, distinguishing merges, recoding, closures and newly opened schools.

leads.title: Meghalaya: audit a sharp one-year reporting change
leads.evidence: Government-school stock moves from 7,789 in 2024-25 to 5,620 in 2025-26, a net difference of −2,169.
leads.nextStep: Reconcile all management categories and school-code transitions before treating the change as an access loss.
leads.claimNotEstablished: 2,169 school closures or a funding irregularity.

leads.title: Telangana: resolve the change in reported government schools
leads.evidence: Government-school stock falls from 30,057 in 2024-25 to 28,088 in 2025-26, a net difference of −1,969.
leads.nextStep: Check comparability and destination capacity before investigating whether particular growth areas have lost accessible seats.
leads.claimNotEstablished: Population growth has outstripped school provision.

leads.title: Uttar Pradesh: trace approved-to-released funding differences
leads.evidence: FY 2025-26 Samagra approved central share ₹5,892.4327 crore versus released ₹5,622.1515 crore; PM SHRI approved ₹377.63 crore versus released ₹236.22 crore.
leads.nextStep: Reconcile sanction ledgers and release conditions across the same fiscal period before attributing delays or calculating school-level spending.
leads.claimNotEstablished: Missing money, misuse or district-level underfunding.

leads.title: Chhattisgarh: preserve revised PAB versions and avoid double counting
leads.evidence: 7 July 2025 revision incorporates supplementary approvals; total plan ₹232,029.17 lakh includes ₹82,492.13 lakh spillover.
leads.nextStep: Link original and revised approvals, label superseded values, and separate spillover, planned releases and actual disbursements.

leads.title: Higher education: compare funding access with government and aided eligibility
leads.evidence: PM-USHA covers government and government-aided state HEIs; AISHE 2023-24 reports 17.1% government, 12.9% private aided and 70.0% private unaided among responding colleges.
leads.nextStep: Join approved institutions to AISHE IDs and eligible categories, then compare underserved district coverage without implying private unaided colleges are entitled to this scheme.
leads.claimNotEstablished: All college types receive comparable government grants.

leads.title: Use child population before flagging closures in growing places
leads.evidence: Official demographic projections allow rising total population alongside falling national ages 5–14 population.
leads.nextStep: Flag only when school/catchment event data and age-specific demand are comparable; display evidence strength and missing inputs.
leads.claimNotEstablished: A general logical contradiction between total population growth and lower school counts.

methodology.geography: Persist geography level and stable identifiers; district, city and catchment are different units. Reconcile boundaries before joining.
methodology.schoolChange: Net stock change = later reported school count − earlier reported count. It is not an event count. Verify closure with an official order and school-code history.
methodology.population: Match the applicable school-age cohort, period, geographic boundary and projection vintage; total-population growth alone is insufficient.
methodology.funding: Keep announced/outlay, budgeted, approved/sanctioned, released/disbursed and expended/utilised separate. Record central/state share, recurring/capital, spillover and opening balance.
methodology.claims: Separate factual observation, investigation lead and substantiated finding. Unknown is not zero; absence of retrieved evidence is not absence of funding.
methodology.provenance: Record source URL, publisher, document date, fiscal/reference period, page/table locator, retrieval date, version and original units.
methodology.dataIntegrity: All 36 state/UT sums reconcile to national government-school totals for all five years; all 75 UP district sums reconcile to UP totals for all five years.

newsCases.title: Uttar Pradesh school pairing: preserve codes and track where classes operate
newsCases.eventStatus: Policy and implementation dispute; historical interim court reporting
newsCases.reportedConcern: Children and parents challenged school pairing and access conditions.
newsCases.governmentResponse: Minister says nearby pairing improves teaching, retains posts and UDISE codes, exempts difficult routes and may be reversed if demand grows.
newsCases.nextCheck: Retrieve latest appellate order and school-wise pairing/restoration list; measure actual class location and travel burden.
newsCases.upgradeIf: Official orders identify affected campuses and current operational status.
newsCases.killIf: Comparable school-level evidence shows no increased access burden or all questioned pairings were restored.

newsCases.title: Honganuru KPS pilot: transport and access require school-level verification
newsCases.eventStatus: Reported seven-school pilot and competing policy descriptions
newsCases.reportedConcern: Student organisations and educationists question rural access from moving classes into a magnet school.
newsCases.governmentResponse: Circular cited in reporting promises transport; minister later says no government schools will be shut.
newsCases.nextCheck: Obtain BEO circular, transfer dates, transport uptime and capacity; distinguish legal school identity from physical location of classes.
newsCases.upgradeIf: Original circular and post-transfer monitoring records are obtained.
newsCases.killIf: Proposed transfers did not occur or verified equivalent access is maintained.

newsCases.title: Himachal rationalisation: separate zero-enrolment denotification from merger
newsCases.eventStatus: Reported completed administrative actions, original orders pending
newsCases.reportedConcern: Consolidation could increase travel burden where nearby school accessibility is weak.
newsCases.governmentResponse: Reported rationale is zero/very low enrolment; difficult-terrain and tribal schools were exempted.
newsCases.nextCheck: Retrieve notifications and receiving-school travel/attendance records; retain100 denotified and120 merged as separate reported actions.
newsCases.upgradeIf: Original notification and institution-level status histories confirm actions.
newsCases.killIf: Notification or exemptions contradict reported counts or affected schools retain service at the same location.
